asof: Settles Fri 20 Nov 2026 · written Sat 21 Nov
headline: AI-led equity rout rallies the reds 16–20bp; U7 peak 4.525%, about 2.5 hikes, now below the three-hike consensus.
summary: SR3 bull-steepened hard as stocks slid: H8 led, 20.5bp lower in rate at 4.415%, with Z7 down 19bp to 4.48%, U7 18.5bp to 4.525%, M7 16.5bp to 4.52% and H7 12.5bp to 4.43%, while Z6 fell only 5bp to 4.24% and U6 edged 0.3bp higher to 3.933%. On the week Z6 is 6.5bp lower, M7 25bp and H8–U8 35–35.5bp, so the month has become a pivot: Z6 and H7 are still 9.5bp and 7.5bp higher than the 30 October settle, U7 is flat (+0.5bp) and Z8 is 8bp lower. U7 remains the peak at 4.525%, 61.5bp over the 3.91% SOFR fixing, with 18bp of easing priced to Z9. That is about two and a half hikes, below the December, January and March path many economists pencil in and closer to CIBC's two hikes or Morgan Stanley's December-then-March call.
drivers: AI-led equity rout sparks a flight to quality

The S&P 500 entered correction territory and Nvidia fell more than 11% after a Reuters report that the SEC is examining its accounting, while Anthropic slipped back toward its IPO price. Cash Treasuries bull-steepened, with 2s down 15.5bp, 5s 16bp and 30s 10.1bp at settlement; in SR3 the move was largest from M7 to U8, at 16.5–20.5bp.

Final November sentiment matched forecasts at 51.5, but year-ahead inflation expectations fell to 3.7% from 4.3% in the preliminary survey and 4.7% in October, and the 5–10-year gauge eased to 3.3% from 3.5%. That undercut the case for hikes beyond the first quarter and helped H7 to U7 fall 12.5–18.5bp.
Fed still hawkish, but 50bp is priced out

Cook backed further hikes, warning that falling behind would mean larger moves later, and Paulson wants more tightening at a deliberate pace; Bessent urged the Fed not to raise by 50bp. Newsquawk noted the market unwound its 50bp pricing for 9 December while keeping 25bp, which is why Z6 fell only 5bp and U6 barely moved; Citi argues the Fed will not want to keep hiking into an equity sell-off.
Supply ahead, funding steady, oil soft on the week

The Treasury sells $69bn of 2s on Monday, $70bn of 5s and $28bn of 2-year FRNs on Tuesday and $44bn of 7s on Wednesday, all coupons settling on 30 November. SOFR fixed at 3.91% on 19 November, 1bp higher and 3bp over EFFR at 3.88%; Brent rose 59 cents to $92.57 and WTI 77 cents to $83.98 on Friday but both posted a third straight weekly loss.
spreads: The curve from the front to the peak flattened sharply as the rally ran from H7 back. U6/Z6 fell 5.3bp to +30.7bp (+8.45bp on the month), Z6/H7 7.5bp to +19bp (−10.5bp week-to-date, −2bp on the month), H7/M7 4bp to +9bp (−8bp on the week, −3.5bp on the month) and M7/U7 2bp to +0.5bp, leaving M7 to U7 almost flat. Past the peak U7/Z7 slipped 0.5bp to −4.5bp, Z7/H8 1.5bp to −6.5bp (−3.5bp on the month) and H8/M8 rose 0.5bp to −4bp, while the 2028–29 spreads rose 0.5–1.5bp to between −2.5bp and +1bp as Z8 onward lagged. Z6/Z7 fell 14bp to +24bp (−25.5bp on the week, −11bp on the month) and Z6/M7 11.5bp to +28bp (−18.5bp on the week, −5.5bp on the month); Z7/Z8 rose 0.5bp to −14bp (−6.5bp on the month), U7/Z8 was unchanged at −18.5bp (−4.5bp on the week, −8.5bp on the month) and Z8/Z9 rose 3.5bp to +0.5bp. The H7/M7/U7 fly fell 2bp to +8.5bp (−3.5bp on the week, flat on the month) and M7/U7/Z7 1.5bp to +5bp (−2bp on the week, −1.5bp on the month).
fed: The latest weekday fed funds futures snapshot, Thursday's, predates Friday's rally: it prices 26.1bp for 9 December (95.7% for 25bp, 4.3% for 50bp), 42bp by January, 57.5bp by March, 69.4bp by June and a 72.5bp peak by September 2027, easing to 67.5bp by December 2027. That compares with 26.8bp, 45bp, 61.6bp, 77.1bp and an 81.5bp peak on Wednesday, 29.6bp, 47bp, 65.8bp, 83.5bp and 90bp a week earlier on 12 November, and 17.6bp, 24bp, 37.3bp, 52.1bp and 57bp at the 30 October month-end: December is up 8.5bp on the month and the peak 15.5bp, but the peak is 17.5bp below a week ago. Adding the 3bp SOFR–EFFR gap, Thursday's ZQ path implies about 4.26% for Z6's December–March window, 4.52% for H7 and 4.62% for U7; Friday's settles sit 2bp, 9bp and 10bp below, so SR3 now prices a peak near 61.5bp over SOFR and the next ZQ snapshot should fall. Many economists still expect hikes in December, January and March, CIBC two and Morgan Stanley December then March, while Citi sees one and then cuts later in 2027; the strip now sits between the two-hike and three-hike camps.

ideas.title: Fade the risk-off rally: sell M7
ideas.why: The Z6/M7 re-sell order at +40bp never filled (the 19 Nov settle was +39.5bp) and the spread has since fallen 11.5bp to +28bp, past our +34bp target, so we cancel it. M7 has now rallied 16.5bp in a day and 25bp on the week to 4.52%, about 10bp below the June-window rate in Thursday's ZQ path, on an equity rout rather than a data shift, while Cook and Paulson still back more hikes. It is 10bp to target against 6.5bp to the stop.
ideas.risk: A deeper AI and credit sell-off that the Fed is seen responding to could push M7 through 95.545 (4.455%).

ideas.title: Sell Z6/Z7 against the M7 short
ideas.trade: Sell SR3Z6, buy SR3Z7 (sell the Z6/Z7 spread) at +24bp
ideas.why: The long Z6/H7 hedge was stopped: the spread fell 7.5bp to +19bp, through the +22bp stop, as H7 rallied 12.5bp against 5bp in Z6. If the sell-off deepens, December and January stay priced while 2027 hikes come out; Z6/Z7 fell 14bp on Friday and 25.5bp on the week to +24bp, so this gains where the core short loses. It is 8bp to target against 5bp to the stop.
ideas.risk: If equities stabilise and PCE runs hot, Z7 would sell off faster than Z6 and push the spread through +29bp.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract into month-end

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: U6 edged 0.3bp higher in rate to 3.933% while the reds rallied 16–20bp, since only its final week follows the 9 December decision. SOFR fixed at 3.91% on 19 November, 1bp higher and 3bp over EFFR at 3.88%, and $183bn of 2-, 5- and 7-year notes settle on 30 November alongside month-end.
ideas.risk: If month-end passes quietly and SOFR slips back to 3.88–3.90%, U6 would gain a couple of bp.

watch: S&P Global flash PMIs; $69bn 2-year note auction
The first test of front-end demand after Friday's rally; a tail would cheapen H7 and M7 and help the core short.
Conference Board consumer confidence; $70bn 5-year and $28bn 2-year FRN auctions
Confidence shows whether the equity rout is hitting households; the 5s gauge appetite for the belly after a 16bp rally.
October PCE prices, Q3 GDP (second estimate), durable goods, jobless claims, Beige Book; $44bn 7-year auction
Core PCE is expected at 0.3% m/m; a firm print would challenge the rally in the reds and Z6/Z7. Last big data day before 9 December.
Thanksgiving: US markets closed (early close Fri 27 Nov)
Thin trading around the holiday can exaggerate moves; the Fed's pre-meeting blackout starts on 28 November.
Balance-sheet window dressing and settlement can lift SOFR fixings and U6.
The last jobs report before the decision; a soft print after rising claims would pull March hikes and M7 lower.
